subject: astronomy
title: Telescopes: Famous Discoveries
welcome_lead: From Galileo's moons to galaxies far away — telescopes change everything.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: Hubble, James Webb, Galileo's moons.
final_note: Every telescope upgrade rewrites part of our cosmic story.

concepts.def: First to use a telescope on the sky, 1609.
Cloud of gas where stars are born.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 1610 Galileo spotted four moons of Jupiter: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. Proof that not everything orbits Earth.
Above the atmosphere, Hubble took stunning images of nebulae and distant galaxies. It changed astronomy after 1990.
The James Webb Space Telescope sees in infrared. It can peer through dust clouds and look back to galaxies from when the universe was young.
